teams.heading: Fiji Rugby confirms interest in recruiting Mark Nawaqanitawase for 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Earlier this month Fiji Rugby confirmed interest in recruiting Mark Nawaqanitawase for the 2027 World Cup, and Les Kiss has also weighed in on the move. The move comes as Jake White takes charge as head coach, chosen from 31 applicants. Fiji are in Pool C at the tournament with Argentina, Canada and Spain, and the World Cup in Australia is only a year away.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item not already run as a lead, and it names a player and a concrete move by Fiji Rugby.

teams.heading: Seb Atkinson and Arthur Clark make England case in Gloucester's Bordeaux display
teams.body: Gloucester's Seb Atkinson and Arthur Clark both pushed their England claims in round one of the Champions Cup, with Clark making a statement against Bordeaux-Bègles. Atkinson kept injecting himself into Gloucester's attack with his playmaking and carrying, while Clark posted eight tackles, seven carries, a try and an assist as the Cherry and Whites could have taken the win. That display should leave Steve Borthwick brimming, though the wider European round left him with questions.

lead.why: A fresh England-focused read on the Champions Cup round, naming two Gloucester players whose displays bear on Borthwick's selection, and it is not the Pearson story already run.

teams.heading: Dan Robson calls Bordeaux's France star 'ridiculous' after Gloucester draw
teams.body: Gloucester's Dan Robson told Planet Rugby that the 36-36 draw with Bordeaux-Bègles left the huddle feeling disappointed, and that last season's Gloucester "potentially" wouldn't have drawn with them. He called his opposite number's 803 kicking metres "ridiculous". Robson had a season at Pau in the Top 14 before returning to England, and he said the Bordeaux game felt "a bit more familiar" for him.

teams.heading: Alex Nankivell commits to Munster until 2029 with Ireland ambitions intact
teams.body: Alex Nankivell has signed a two-year extension tying the New Zealander to Munster until 2029, and the centre's international ambitions are firmly in view. The 29-year-old joined from the Chiefs in 2023, has played 58 times for the province and was named Munster's 2026 Men's Player of the Year. He will be 32 when he completes World Rugby's residency rules in 2028. Munster general manager Ian Costello says the province hopes to see him "realise that potential in the near future."

lead.why: A contract extension with named players and a clear Ireland angle is harder team news than the already-run squad story or Greenwood's pundit take.

teams.heading: Italy have no wins from three after 10-57 defeat to Australia
teams.body: Italy's 10-57 loss to Australia in Round three leaves them with no wins from three matches. Across those three, they have scored 37 points and conceded 131, a difference of -94. Round four brings South Africa, the reigning world champions, who beat Italy 32-14 at home in November 2025 and are next on the fixture list.

teams.heading: Scotland women's Aicha Sutcliffe makes first start in Canberra against Australia
teams.body: Scotland women's interim head coach Dave Butcher has made Aicha Sutcliffe's first Scotland start one of three changes for the final WXV Global Series match against Australia in Canberra. The Glasgow hooker already has six caps off the bench. Sarah Bonar returns in the second row after missing the 56-12 defeat in Sydney through illness, while Chloe Rollie is back at full-back. Hannah Ramsay moves to fly-half and Helen Nelson to inside centre.

lead.why: The freshest item in the pack with named players, and the men's candidates had already been run.

teams.heading: Tandy leaves out Macs Page despite four tries in four Scarlets appearances
teams.body: Scarlets centre Macs Page is among the most eye-catching omissions from Steve Tandy's 39-man squad, despite four tries in four appearances this season. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies said of the 21-year-old: "He's probably the first name on the team sheet." Davies added: "Steve will definitely be considering him." RUCK reports Page has received an offer from Munster, with no update since, and WalesOnline says he is likely to be the next cab off the rank if injuries strike.

lead.why: A new squad-snub story with a named Wales player and a Scarlets quote, and the Faletau item has already run.

teams.heading: Argentina lead four-nation South American bid to host 2035 Rugby World Cup
teams.body: Argentina are leading a joint South American bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, with Uruguay, Chile and Brazil joining them in the submission. Planet Rugby frames the proposal as a direct challenge to World Rugby's desire for a European return, making Argentina's case a test of how far the sport's governing body will look beyond Europe. World Rugby has yet to select the host, so the bid stays live until that decision lands.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson admits 'so much pressure' from All Blacks in Bledisloe losses
teams.body: Wallabies captain Harry Wilson said after Saturday's second Bledisloe Test, a 43-21 loss in Sydney, that he 'probably never felt under so much pressure as in the last two games' against the All Blacks. Wilson and Fraser McReight are confident of doing well on the Nations Championship tour, which opens against England at Twickenham and also takes in Scotland and Wales. McReight said the Wallabies would have taken an undefeated Bledisloe series going in, and called the All Blacks 'world-class for a reason'.

lead.why: It is a fresh angle on the Bledisloe fallout (Wilson and McReight, not the Matfield take already run) and it looks ahead to the northern tour.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One softens proposed rules restricting foreign-born players with Japanese passports
teams.body: On 28 August, Japan Rugby League One backed down on proposed registration rules that would have restricted players holding Japanese passports but born abroad. Players who gained Japanese nationality before the end of May 2025 will now be treated the same as Japanese-born players when the 2026-27 season opens in December. Among the players who sued was Timothy Lafaele, who starred for Japan at the 2019 World Cup. The climbdown follows a backlash from players and fans, a league executive admitting it had underestimated the reaction.

lead.why: The Smith and sevens stories have already run, and this is the only remaining Japan rugby item in the pack that names players and a clear decision.

teams.heading: All Blacks go out early to acknowledge Nathan Charles before Sydney Test
teams.body: On Saturday in Sydney, the All Blacks left the dressing room a couple of minutes early so they could go and see Nathan Charles on the field. The former Wallabies hooker, 37, recently revealed his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis, and the whole team went over to him, shook his hand and hugged him before the All Blacks' 43-21 win. Both teams united in support of Charles, and captain Codie Taylor presented him with a framed All Blacks jersey signed by the squad.

lead.why: A fresh team-level story about the All Blacks' conduct, which outranks the pundit verdicts and the already-run McKenzie item.

teams.heading: Warren Whiteley confirms Springboks have joined Sharks ahead of Cardiff clash
teams.body: Several Springboks have joined the Sharks ahead of Friday's URC clash against Cardiff at the Arms Park, forwards coach Warren Whiteley confirmed on Tuesday. Captain André Esterhuizen, Edwill van der Merwe, Ethan Hooker, Ox Nché and Thomas du Toit were rested for last Saturday's 40-33 away win against Lyon, and Whiteley said the group has had only one session together. He knows of no injury concerns, adding that they are all available and all flew across.

lead.why: It is the strongest new squad item in the pack, with named Springboks and a confirmed availability update, which outranks the Kitshoff pundit take.
